item.title: CFTC charges North Carolina commodity pool operator and company with fraud involving crypto assets and equity index futures ($14M+, 60+ victims)
item.category: CFTC
item.description:
On July 7, 2026, the CFTC filed a civil enforcement complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of North Carolina (Press Release 9264-26) against Trevor L. Vernon and Argent Capital Management LLC. The complaint alleges that from approximately March 2022 through February 2026, Vernon and Argent Capital solicited approximately $14 million from more than 60 participants for a commodity pool that purported to trade equity index futures contracts, options on equity index futures, and crypto assets, among other purported investments. The CFTC alleges Vernon misappropriated pool funds and operated a Ponzi-like scheme, making lulling payments to earlier participants with funds from newer investors. The complaint seeks restitution, civil monetary penalties, disgorgement, and permanent trading and registration bans.
Primary source: CFTC Press Release 9264-26 (July 7, 2026; primary source retrieved) — https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9264-26

item.title: Nevada Supreme Court denies Kalshi's emergency stay, leaving geofencing mandate in force as July 16 contempt hearing is set
item.category: Nevada Supreme Court
item.description:
As reported by CoinDesk and Tech Times (July 5, 2026), the Nevada Supreme Court on or about July 1, 2026 denied KalshiEx, LLC's emergency motion for a stay pending appeal, so Kalshi must continue to geofence and block Nevada users from prohibited event contracts while the state's lawsuit proceeds. Per the coverage, a three-justice panel (Linda Marie Bell, Ron D. Parraguirre, and Kristina Pickering) said it was 'not persuaded' by the emergency motion. Separately, the Nevada Gaming Control Board has asked the First Judicial District Court to hold Kalshi in contempt for allegedly failing to geofence the state, and a full-day evidentiary hearing on that question is scheduled for July 16, 2026.

item.title: North Carolina budget deal (SB 257) adds a 6% tax on prediction-market trading-fee revenue, without bringing platforms under state gambling rules
item.category: North Carolina General Assembly
item.description:
As reported by CoinDesk and Tech Times (July 5, 2026) and corroborated by WRAL and Bloomberg Tax, North Carolina lawmakers included a 6% tax on prediction-market operators' net in-state trading-fee revenue in the state's roughly $34 billion conference budget bill (SB 257), reported the week of June 30-July 2, 2026. Per the coverage, the tax would take effect in 2027 and apply to platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket, but the budget language does not place prediction-market platforms under North Carolina's gambling licensing, know-your-customer, or responsible-gaming rules; the same budget raises the state's online sports-betting tax from 18% to 23%.

item.title: SCOTUS rules 6-3 that for-cause removal protections for SEC and CFTC commissioners are unconstitutional (Trump v. Slaughter, No. 25-332)
item.category: U.S. Supreme Court
item.description:
On June 29, 2026, the Supreme Court of the United States issued its 6-3 opinion in Trump v. Slaughter (No. 25-332), authored by Chief Justice Roberts, overturning Humphrey's Executor v. United States (1935). The Court held that the for-cause removal protection in the FTC's enabling statute — and by structural extension the SEC and CFTC, which operate under identical removal provisions — is contrary to the separation of powers under the Constitution. Effective immediately, the President may remove SEC and CFTC commissioners without cause. A companion order in Trump v. Cook (No. 25A312, June 29, 2026) denied a government application to stay a preliminary injunction protecting Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook; the Federal Reserve's statutory structure was not directly addressed by the majority opinion. The opinion is published on the Court's official slip opinion list for October Term 2025.
Primary source: U.S. Supreme Court — Official Slip Opinion List, October Term 2025 (primary source; retrieved July 3, 2026); Opinion PDF: https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/25pdf/25-322_new_4gcj.pdf — https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/slipopinion/25
Relevant to: crypto exchanges, digital asset issuers, fintech platforms, prediction-market operators, CFTC-registered entities, and all operators subject to SEC or CFTC jurisdiction

item.title: Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) misses July 4 Senate floor vote target as bipartisan talks collapse
item.category: U.S. Senate
item.description:
As of July 2, 2026, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) did not receive a Senate floor vote before the July 4 recess deadline targeted by White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt. According to the Bitcoin Foundation (July 2, 2026; corroborated by Elliptic, Crypto.news, PYMNTS, and Yahoo Finance/BeInCrypto), bipartisan negotiations failed to secure the minimum 7 Democratic votes needed to clear the Senate's 60-vote cloture threshold. Outstanding disputes included DeFi oversight provisions, stablecoin rewards provisions, AML reporting requirements, and Section 604 (Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act). The bill remains on the Senate Legislative Calendar (General Orders, Calendar No. 423) and is not dead; a floor vote has been pushed to after the July 4 recess at earliest. Multiple trade outlets reported prediction market passage odds fell from approximately 74% approximately one month prior to approximately 48% as of the July 2 reporting date.
Coverage: Bitcoin Foundation, July 2, 2026 (corroborated by Elliptic, Crypto.news, PYMNTS, Yahoo Finance/BeInCrypto) — https://bitcoinfoundation.org/news/regulation/clarity-act-blocked-before-july-4-senate-delay-sparks-uncertainty-what-happens-next/
Relevant to: crypto exchanges, token platforms, stablecoin issuers, DeFi protocols, fintech and payments operators awaiting US market structure clarity

item.title: OFAC adds Monero (XMR) and 100+ TRON addresses to ISIS-K SDN entry; designates Brazilian payments company Pixwave under SDGT and narco-trafficking EO
item.category: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
item.description:
On July 1, 2026, OFAC published two actions on its recent-actions page. First, OFAC updated the existing SDGT entry for ISIS-K to add three Monero (XMR) cryptocurrency wallet addresses and more than 100 TRON (TRC-20) blockchain addresses — including USDT-TRC20 stablecoin addresses — to the SDN List. Second, OFAC designated Pixwave Soluções de Pagamentos Ltda, a Brazilian payment-technology company, under the SDGT authority (E.O. 13224) and Executive Order 14059 (ILLICIT-DRUGS-EO14059), alleging Pixwave provided payment-processing services to the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), a Brazilian narco-trafficking organization. Both designations are effective July 1, 2026.
Primary source: OFAC Recent Actions — July 1, 2026 (primary source; retrieved) — https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20260701
Relevant to: crypto exchanges, virtual asset service providers (VASPs), payment processors, money transmitters, and any US person transacting in Monero or TRON-chain assets (including USDT-TRC20)

item.title: SEC seeks public comment on registration and disclosure rules for novel exchange-traded funds (Release 33-11426) — crypto-asset and event-contract ETFs expressly in scope
item.category: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
item.description:
On June 30, 2026, the SEC released Release 33-11426, a request for public comment on potential amendments to its registration and disclosure rules for novel types of exchange-traded funds, including crypto-asset ETFs and ETFs holding event-contract or prediction-market exposures. The release asks whether current disclosure frameworks adequately address risks specific to non-standard ETF product types and whether the Commission should take additional steps, including potential Commission-initiated delay of automatic effectiveness of registration statements under Rule 485. Comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication.

item.title: Kalshi files federal lawsuit against Illinois over SB3019's 15% sports prediction market gross receipts tax and state licensing requirement for DCMs; TRO and PI sought ahead of July 1 effective date
item.category: KalshiEx LLC (plaintiff) v. Governor JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, Illinois Gaming Board — U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois
item.description:
Kalshi filed a 31-page federal complaint in the N.D. Illinois on June 23, 2026. SB3019 imposes: (a) a 15% gross-receipts tax on sports prediction market revenues; (b) a state licensing requirement for CFTC-registered DCMs. Both provisions took effect July 1, 2026. Kalshi argues both provisions are preempted by the Commodity Exchange Act's exclusive-jurisdiction clause (7 U.S.C. § 2(a)(1)(A)). The complaint seeks a TRO, preliminary injunction, and permanent injunction.
